testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a heavy load is slowing you down, where should you drive?
questions.correctAnswerText: In the right lane.
questions.explanation: The right lane is for slower-moving vehicles. If your heavy load is slowing you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: If you see lights while driving in fog, what should you know?

options.text: The lights are definitely on the road.
The lights might be a reflection.
The lights might be an optical illusion.
The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have pulled off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have pulled off the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not reliable guides to where the road is. The lights you see may come from a vehicle that has left the road.

questions.question: When should you test the low pressure warning signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Test your low pressure warning light before each trip. Let the system charge first. Then quickly press and release the brake pedal several times to release air from the brakes. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: How much water is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A large amount, like a big puddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. This can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.question: What is a header board used for?

options.text: To help the driver see behind them.
To protect the driver from moving cargo.
To keep the driver from leaving the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the driver from moving cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board (also called a headache rack) is a barrier at the front of a truck. It protects the driver from cargo that shifts or falls forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: All cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down. This prevents it from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: What should you do during the on-road driving test?

options.text: Create your own route to show off your skills.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the examiner's directions.
questions.explanation: During the test, listen to and follow all directions from the examiner. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes too much.
questions.explanation: When you use the brakes too much, they overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: What is a problem with rough acceleration?

options.text: It helps keep you awake on long trips.
It can damage the engine and transmission.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration makes the vehicle jerk and can cause mechanical damage.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, your braking distance becomes how many times longer?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four times longer.
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance increases by four times. The impact force in a crash also multiplies by four.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to remove the vehicle from the tracks.
Walk down the tracks to look for a train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, get out immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services right away.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn frequently while driving, you should:

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Frequent yawning means you are getting tired. The only safe thing to do is stop and sleep. Coffee and other stimulants only work for a short time and will make you more tired later.

questions.question: How can you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down and release it. If it does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down and release it. If it squeaks, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when you press the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times. Then press hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another brake problem.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the right distance behind the driver.
Keeps a safe distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. A damaged suspension system is dangerous.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, you should stay at least how many seconds behind the vehicle ahead?
questions.correctAnswerText: Six seconds.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and applying the parking brake.
The vehicle touching an exercise boundary line.
A driver completing an exercise correctly.
An applicant trying to bribe the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during an exercise. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: A vehicle inspection is required:
questions.correctAnswerText: By state and federal law.
questions.explanation: State and federal laws require commercial vehicle drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to change gears. Release the gas, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral at the same time. Release the clutch and let the engine speed change. Then push in the clutch, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should check that the spring brakes turn on automatically when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that spring brakes engage automatically when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air by pressing the brake pedal on and off. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should activate.

questions.question: If someone pulls in front of you and you cannot stop in time, you should:

options.text: Hit the other vehicle since it is their fault.
Swerve to avoid the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerve to avoid the other car.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle pulls in front of you, brake if you have room to stop. If you do not have room to stop, swerving may be the safer choice.

questions.question: After starting a trip with cargo, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to inspect the cargo.
Only inspect the cargo if it is making noise.
Only inspect the cargo if there is an obvious problem.
Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: When you enter a foggy area, you should:

options.text: Stop on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Always slow down when entering fog. Use low beam headlights. Do not pass other vehicles or stop on the side of the road. If possible, avoid driving in fog completely.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed.
To remove bad air from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and oil. These substances can damage brakes if they build up. Drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:

options.text: Not recommended because it can damage your vehicle.
Not recommended because it may confuse other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because it can damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause your vehicle to jerk and damage it.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what is the safest option?

options.text: Follow the vehicle ahead of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive in fog.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see the road, other drivers, and hazards. Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tight.
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. The right amount of tightness depends on your vehicle, so learn what is correct for your engine.

questions.question: What can happen if you use parking brakes in very wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.
The brakes may become too smooth to work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in very wet weather when it is freezing. The brakes can freeze in place and keep the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, you should:

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Not wear gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant. Use gloves or a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, which of the following should you NOT check?

options.text: The coolant level in the radiator.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fuel level.
questions.explanation: Check the oil level, coolant level, hose condition, power steering fluid, windshield washer fluid, battery condition and connections, transmission fluid, and belt condition. Also check for leaks and worn wiring. Do not check the fuel level during an engine compartment inspection.

questions.question: A vehicle's center of gravity height:

options.text: Usually has no effect on how the vehicle handles.
Is very important to safe handling.
Does not matter when loading the vehicle.
Only matters on routes with many hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important to safe handling.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity height affects how safely you can handle it. Always place cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that looks black because of dirt on the road
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet, not icy.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs you need to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two tie-downs
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, no matter how small, must have at least two tie-downs.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, you should:

options.text: Hope the vehicle lasts until another driver takes over.
Stop and check the vehicle to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the vehicle to find the problem.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, stop right away and inspect your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, is it important to keep space between your vehicle and other vehicles?

options.text: No, it is a waste of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is important.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your vehicle and others is essential for safety. This space lets you stop safely without hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, what should you NOT do with your gears?

options.text: Select a gear that makes the engine rev too much
Shift while going through an intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift while turning
questions.explanation: Pick a gear that does not make the engine rev or strain. Avoid grinding gears. Do not shift while turning or going through intersections.

questions.question: What is tire load?

options.text: The highest air pressure a tire can hold
The heaviest weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure
The lightest weight a tire can safely carry
The average weight of all tires on a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure
questions.explanation: Tire load is the heaviest weight a tire can safely carry at a set pressure. This number is printed on the side of the tire.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do with turn signals?

options.text: You do not need to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Only use them if another vehicle is next to you.
Do not use them if your lane change is obvious.
Always use them to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use them to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals so other drivers know your plans.

questions.question: What might it mean if a vehicle stops at a green light?

options.text: The driver may not know the traffic rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may be impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have had alcohol, drugs, lack sleep, or are ill are dangerous. Stopping at green lights is a sign someone may be impaired.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, what should you check on the hoses?

options.text: That they are connected to the battery
That they have the right amount of movement

questions.correctAnswerText: For leaks
questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels in a power steering system. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal, then the left turn signal
Tap your brake pedal several times to flash the brake lights
Swerve side to side to get their attention
Turn all lights on and off many times

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal several times to flash the brake lights
questions.explanation: To alert drivers behind you that you are slowing down, tap your brake pedal lightly several times. This makes your brake lights flash.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Do not check your mirrors for other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When you need to turn quickly to avoid a crash, always keep both hands on the steering wheel. A firm grip helps you turn fast.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a type of retarder?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake use. The four main types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Challenge them.
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, your best choice is to get out of their way. Do not provoke them with eye contact, racing, or refusing to move. Ignore any rude gestures.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, what should a driver do?

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving only at certain times.
Honk to make other drivers move out of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving only at certain times.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or heavy loads need special permits. These loads may only be allowed on the road at certain times of day.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a way to reduce driving distractions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Eat while driving
questions.explanation: To avoid distractions, pre-program your radio, plan your route ahead of time, and adjust your mirrors before you leave. Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: What is true about emergency brakes?

options.text: They are not required on trucks.
They are only required on trailers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required on tractors.
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must work using mechanical force.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid
questions.explanation: Check for brake problems like cracked drums, shoes or pads covered with oil or grease, and shoes that are broken or worn too thin.

questions.question: Why should mirrors show part of your vehicle as well as the road behind you?

options.text: Showing only the road would make the driver carsick.
Seeing part of your truck helps you judge distances to other vehicles.
It is illegal to show only the road in your mirrors.
You need to see reflections of vehicles on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing part of your truck helps you judge distances to other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle should be visible in your mirrors. This gives you a reference point to judge how close other drivers and objects are to you.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one brake use.
Hold enough air for several brake uses if the compressor fails.
Only hold air during an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 brake uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several brake uses if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the storage tanks hold enough air so brakes can be used several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: What can happen with improperly loaded cargo?

options.text: It looks bad to others on the road.
It can injure the driver during a quick stop.
It makes it easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can injure the driver during a quick stop.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly loaded and secured so it does not fall or shift. During a quick stop, loose cargo can injure or kill the driver.
